memoryReview.lesson: Dungeon turns and overhead board representation work there, but repeat neither the grid framing nor the touch d-pad.
A first-person action setting can use dynamic geometry, but this survival game should not imitate weapon-dominated HUD and combat.

references.observation: Original 2D map uses independently regenerated tile chunks and a limited memory-visibility duration.
references.principle: Architecture rearranging itself behind the player is the central gameplay identity, not merely random corridors.
references.application: Whole sectors regenerate after being left behind with fixed guaranteed edge portals and a deterministic seed.
references.avoid: Avoid partial merging of old remembered cells into new grids, which was able to strand walking paths.

references.observation: The Godot prototype already started experimenting with spatial movement, apartment cells, and projectile scripts.
references.principle: Player-scale spatial navigation fits the tension of a horror labyrinth better than reading square tiles from above.
references.application: Build directly authored WebGL polygons with eye-height look and actual collisions, not a visual-only 2D mockup.
references.avoid: Do not carry over engine-specific scene dependencies or half-connected controllers from the abandoned prototype.

references.observation: Existing Gloamstep demonstrates a fully localized mobile dungeon, objective counters and a deliberate exit route.
references.principle: On a small screen, important progress and escape should be visible without permanent panels or scrolling.
references.application: Place only health, memory counter, nearest target compass and pause above the full-bleed geometry.
references.avoid: Avoid copying overhead tile rendering, the framing strips or a full directional control pad.

concepts.medium: Offline native WebGL 1 polygons with a custom flashlight shader and depth-tested concrete geometry.
concepts.composition: The environment occupies the whole phone, with a narrow permanent compass and peripheral twin-thumb controls.
concepts.interaction: A drag steers the head independently from movement; players cross real gates, lose sight of old routes, and find signals.
concepts.motion: Immediate first-person turning and proportional walking bob; distant corridors softly fade through atmospheric fog.
concepts.rationale: Chosen because changing spaces are felt bodily at eye level and all needed resources are local on slow mobile networks.

concepts.medium: High-resolution 2D canvas and charcoal ink corridors rendered as an architectural memory diagram.
concepts.composition: Top-down floor plan drawn onto a stationary document with side navigation and a map scanner.
concepts.interaction: The player drags a cursor on the blueprint, while ink erases and redraws areas outside a radial sight cone.
concepts.motion: Ink wash evaporates in slow paper-grain transitions, leaving scratches before returning to the document.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because the old 2D presentation already obscured personal vulnerability and the sense of scale.

concepts.medium: CSS perspective projections of a paper diorama with separately articulated cardboard walls and doors.
concepts.composition: A central miniature room suspended between vertically arranged navigation documents and object descriptions.
concepts.interaction: Players physically rotate a cardboard room, then choose doors by tapping miniature handles one room at a time.
concepts.motion: Cardboard walls fold on hinges with a spring settling and paper-slot transition to the next isolated scene.
concepts.rationale: Rejected because one-room-at-a-time jumps weaken continuous navigation and make the world feel like a puzzle box.

selection.reason: True perspective supports the original memory-shifting idea while a fixed connected graph avoids recreating the old navigation failures.

rejected.reason: A legible overhead plan would be a clearer editor, but loses the horror of not seeing behind the player.
Hand-built CSS cardboard cannot affordably stream the corridors and continuous depth this mechanic depends on.

tools.reason: WebGL context, shaders, vertex buffers and geometric occlusion are implemented directly in renderer.mjs.
A custom vector double-portal emblem was authored for the launcher icon with a clear at-a-glance silhouette.
Native Node test runner can exercise connected portals and navigation across seeds without a browser.

assets.role: Recognizable square app emblem where a narrow signal glows deep behind a concrete double gate.
assets.acceptance: The stacked doorway and warm beacon remain distinct as a single app icon at 64 pixels.
assets.integration: The launcher, manifest, HTML and offline service worker all reference the same local SVG.
assets.provenance: Hand-authored from original paths and gradients for this project, without third-party art or font binaries.

assets.role: Procedural lit walls, ceiling slabs, floor joints, memory monoliths and pursuer silhouettes define the actual space.
assets.acceptance: Cells share matching exits and the renderer draws depth-tested triangles with flashlight shading and fog.
assets.integration: The renderer reads chunk geometry from World and draws cached WebGL meshes plus dynamic actors.
assets.provenance: All primitives, palette, lighting formula and world topology are original local JavaScript source.

evidence.firstFrame: First-person corridor preview under a large compressed title and rotated mechanical aperture.
evidence.action: Entering the labyrinth removes the menu and the user immediately walks through spatial corridors.
evidence.settled: A memory signal vanishes on approach, the progress counter increments and compass redirects.

risks: Shader compile error, WebGL context loss or a missing mobile touch pointer could leave a black frame.
Long controls on a narrow phone must never obscure the next memory marker or block the real gameplay.
Sectors may regenerate only after the player leaves, without sealing portals or spawning actors inside walls.
comparisons: GLOAMSTEP uses top-down flat tiles while this app uses eye-level volumetric corridors and no d-pad.
MELT//CRYPT is a weapon-centric action arena rather than navigational horror without combat equipment.
Axis Pals is a planar shared-control puzzle rather than a solo first-person exploration space.
